title: Certified does not always mean approved by your utility
description: Use the utility's official tester rule first, then use a commercial provider path only when it does not conflict with that rule.
answer: A tester may hold a state or county credential and still need utility registration, an official-list placement, portal enrollment, insurance, calibration records, or a narrower device scope.
urgency: Booking the wrong tester can leave a completed test unaccepted. Match the tester to the exact utility before the appointment.
diagramAlt: Tester credential flow from certification through utility approval and portal submission
identifiers: Official list: published or linked by the governing utility.
Registration gate: the tester must enroll with the city or utility.
Portal gate: accepted submission may require an authorized tester account.

choices.label: My utility publishes an official list
choices.detail: Use that list as the primary route.

choices.label: The notice names a portal
choices.detail: Check both the utility rule and portal enrollment requirement.

choices.label: No official list is published
choices.detail: A provider search can help, but verify credentials with the utility.

choices.label: The test already failed
choices.detail: Look for repair authorization and retest eligibility too.

steps.title: Name the governing utility
steps.body: City boundaries and water-service boundaries are not always the same.

steps.title: Read the eligibility language
steps.body: Look for approved, registered, certified, accepted, portal-enrolled, or device-scope limits.

steps.title: Confirm before booking
steps.body: Ask the tester to confirm the utility and who will submit the result.

safeChecks: Open the official utility source, not a copied directory.
Confirm the tester's name or company matches the accepted credential.
Ask whether the tester files the report.
Keep the appointment, report, and acceptance confirmation together.
stopConditions: The provider claims every utility accepts the same credential
The official list is expired or undated
The tester will not identify the filing route
notThisDevice: A nationwide directory can be useful discovery but is not an authority.
A plumbing license alone may not satisfy the backflow tester gate.
Portal access does not replace professional or utility eligibility.

related.title: Find the utility from the notice
